claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features microtransactions and a battle pass system.

citations.review_text:
Chivalry 2 is one of those games that pisses me off to no end.

Before I go off on my rant here, the core game is amazing. The devs on the ground floor clearly have passion and experience in their craft. It's not the animators fault the game is designed this way, and that needs to be said.

Because what we have here is an insanely fun game with unique level design, wonderful combat, great animation, and great well....everything. A game that I am having a ton of fun playing.

But then that awesome core game is wrapped around a greedy, live service, monetize everything, design scheme that really gets under my skin. And in the case of Chivalry 2 there a few details that are INSANELY infuriating with this one, and even though I have fun playing, it still leaves behind a sour aftertaste that doesn't go away.

It only took me a few levels ups to realize the progression system is essentially non-existent. Don't get me wrong, there are tons of armor pieces, unlockables, etc. But every single one of them are tied to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ schemes.

Chivalry 2 has four factions, or teams, you can end up playing as. Minus a couple side game modes, each match will only have 2 of those teams in play. Depending on the game mode, or certain server circumstances, sometimes you are allowed to switch to the other team. But this isn't always the case, and even still, there are only 2 of the 4 factions you can pick in any given match. So, what team you play on is kinda random for the most part. You can't really have a favorite faction and always play as them, etc. Also, each of the teams share the same identical classes you can pick. (Knight, archer, etc)

Why is that important? Because all the items and cusomizations you can buy, are tied to a single class of a single faction. So if your favorite class is the knight, and you mostly play as the knight, you'll then also be unlocking and buying items for the knight. However, you can end up playing as any of the 4 factions randomly. So, if you have a w…

A £36 game with a battlepass and microtransactions. 
No private servers unless you rent them from the devs. 

'nuff said.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe severe server latency and performance issues that negatively impact directional swordplay and hit registration.

citations.review_text:
I want to like this game, but unfortunately, it’s going to be a no from me.

At this point, you’re dealing with servers that run like garbage, even when your ping looks perfectly fine. The latency is bad enough that it genuinely affects swordplay, which makes an already difficult combat system even more frustrating.

On top of that, you’ll regularly run into people with literally thousands of hours who have been playing since launch and apparently treat this game like a full-time career, lmao. If you’re not willing to sink hundreds of hours into mastering an already basically dead game, you might have some fun here and there, but eventually you’ll realize you could just be playing something better with significantly less jank.

There’s a decent game buried in here somewhere, but the balance is terrible. There are basically two metas, and if you aren’t playing one of them, you’re probably going to get absolutely wrecked. Combine that with the bad servers, latency issues, and an extremely hardcore veteran player base that can be incredibly toxic, and it makes the game really hard to recommend to anyone who’s never played it before.

And I mean, let’s be real... this game is advertised as a first person slasher, but every sweat just plays in third person so they can abuse crazy drags and maximize their damage. At that point, it feels like you’re not even playing the game the way it was advertised. The first person combat is supposed to be the selling point, yet the optimal way to play is basically to pull the camera into third person and exploit every possible animation advantage.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game features multiple campaigns requiring separate premium passes, along with cosmetic items and gear locked behind paywalls or a progression grind.

citations.review_text:
Likes:
- fun combat that is decently intuitive, with a very high skill ceiling 
- a wide variety of weapons and skins for those weapons
- a LOT of armors (cosmetic) that are locked behind progression 
- I have not experienced major bugs, or a lot of bugs during gameplay

Neutral:
- the community can be hit or miss, but I have not felt like this community was particularly aggressive over anything (in game chat)

Dislikes:
- horses are really strong
- the short sword should have some better cosmetics
- some cosmetics are for FFA mode only, but that mode goes through a rotation (with some others) and isn't always available.
- some of the better cosmetics are locked behind pay walls. The way I dealt with this was to get the DLCs when they were on sale for a dollar each, and that gave me enough of the paid currency to get most of the stuff I wanted
- progressing can feel a little grindy at times, and starting out without most of the classes unlocked sucked

Chivalry 2 is, in its best moments, a fun beta for a better game. On average it struggles to be engaging and the unpolished most basic gameplay mechanics prevent you from focusing on enjoying the action. 
The worst aspect is the in-game chat. If you thought you had seen it all, heard it all in some toxic FPS lobby, I don't think you can fathom the obscene, childish, malignant tumor represented by a sizeable chunk of this game's player base. 

If you want a paid sightseeing experience of the zoo, and you're ready to look past a superficial, unpolished, crude moneygrab with not one, but multiple premium passes required, one per campaign (each composed of the same repeating multiplayer maps over and over) and  you're also fine with an explicitly labeled 'offline' experience that requires you to be online... be my guest. If you have better ways to spend your cash, I highly suggest you stay clear of this medieval-adjacent second-rate cesspool of unmoderated trolls.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks skill-based matchmaking, resulting in matches against experienced high-level players.

citations.review_text:
This game is cool at first. The mechanics and gameplay is genuinely fun. It can be as hilarious and it is cinematic. The community isn't too bad. A few different game modes for whatever it is you are looking for. However, overtime the cons start to outweigh the pros.

1. There is no matchmaking. Literally just finished a game that had 4 people at level 1000 on the enemy team and mine capped out at maybe 4-500? I wish that was an uncommon thing but it ain't. It is not friendly to new or returning players. You either grind or you don't and it will show. 

2. For a team game on mass scale, there is NO coordination. If you like to play OBJ you will be one of few doing so. If you don't, I can respect the hack-and-slash but your game will be over before you know it which will in turn end your personal crusade. Thus, your game will be over TOO quickly and you will probably lose. You can't really make call outs because everyone does their own thing. There is 0 strategy so you either win or you don't. 

3. The fighting is cool. Epic even. Whether you enjoy honorable 1v1's, Free-for-All, or mass warfare it CAN be there. But in most cases, it is not. Somehow, someway, you are constantly outnumbered. You could be in the middle of the scrap, your battle line against theirs. Yet your team will disappear and you will be engulfed by your opponents. This is constant. A lot of players don't really fight to fight anymore. They run around you to flank you on all sides, finish you and then move on to the next or vice-versa. This is not fun for either party. You can't contest skill. Even if you are in a 1v1 or 1v2, someone will see that as an invitation and assume you are lonely only to turn that into a 1v7 for some reason. Again, I do not know why, but this is also consistent. Try defending? That kinda goes well. But all good things come to an end but rather quickly in this game. 

There are some other minor ordeals but I don't think they are as important as these 3 personally. I can ov…

Unless they make the ranked matchmaking system, I'm not recommending this game. I'm tired of getting into lobbies with level 1000 players against whom I have no chance. If you're new to this game, be prepared to be constantly killed by players that have hundreds or even thousands of hours without a way to play with people of your own rank.

citations.review_text: This game feels like a callback to an older era of gaming where games didn't take themselves so seriously. The combat is easy to learn but hard to master, but feels very rewarding to get good at. They removed almost all of the cheese of Chivalry I and Mordhau from the weapon inertia so it actually looks and feels like a fight. There's a lot of hidden easter eggs and funny voice lines where you can tell that the devs had a blast making this game. The maps can get a bit samey after a while since the devs pushed out their final major update a while ago, but the game is still very much worth your time. The chat can be toxic, but I still regularly get fun moments in my matches where everyone gets together and listens to a bard play a harp or spam laugh emotes at the peasant NPCs. Great game

[h1]Still the best medieval slasher[/h1]

As someone who spent [b]hundreds of hours in Chivalry 1[/b], I took my time when Chivalry 2 was announced and only dropped in a couple years after its launch. Thankfully, it still absolutely delivers.

The combat is satisfying, the maps are chaotic in all the right ways, the soundtrack (I'm guessing Celestial Aeon Project like in Chiv 1 ?) is genuinely excellent, and the whole game embraces that wonderfully stupid [i]Monty Python[/i]-style medieval humor without taking itself too seriously. One moment you're leading a glorious charge, the next you're throwing a chicken at someone while screaming battle cries.

[b]The biggest shame?[/b] It feels like the developers abandoned it far too soon. This game deserved years more support because it's [u]still absolutely worth playing[/u].

Whether you're here to casually bonk knights after work or spend hours mastering drags, feints, counters and footwork, Chivalry 2 has something for you. It somehow manages to be approachable and surprisingly deep at the same time.

It's not perfect. Public servers are [strike]completely free of cheaters[/strike] [i]occasionally polluted by hackers and cheaters[/i], which can be frustrating. Thankfully they're not common enough to ruin the experience, but they're there.

Also brace yourselves for in-game chat, as the lads don't tend to use any filters.

As for the eternal comparison:
[list]
[*][b]Mordhau[/b] wins when it comes to cosmetics and customization.
[*][b]Chivalry 2[/b] wins where it matters most: gameplay.
[/list]

Would I recommend it?

[b]Absolutely.[/b]

Now back to swinging.
